meta.title: KV Cache Compression: The Recovery Bottleneck
meta.subtitle: A reproducible research meeting demo · Qwen3-32B / TP4

slides.title: Compression is not free.
body: A reported 72.7% storage reduction coincides with slower recovery in this setup.
slides.notes: Open with the tradeoff. Present values as preliminary observations until logs and repetitions are verified.

slides.title: Reported compression does not imply a faster first token.
body: Raw Hit TTFT P50 is 0.353s; BitPack4 compressed Hit is 67.792s.
The performance gap motivates critical-path measurement, not claims about the final codec.

slides.title: Reported storage savings need verification; latency needs explanation.
Reported BitPack4 hit TTFT is higher in this single setup.
body: These are one setup's reported P50 values, not a distribution or uncertainty estimate.

slides.title: Instrument the complete recovery path before optimizing components.
body: The per-part host decode timing cannot be compared directly with full-request TTFT without part counts and overlap analysis.

slides.title: Three controlled checks can localize the bottleneck.
body: Trace per-part latency and critical-path stalls
Compare sequential and batched recovery under matched workloads
Verify post-reload correctness before performance claims

slides.title: Prioritize recovery profiling over a higher compression ratio.
body: Proposed next step: paired, repeatable tests with decode/transfer/sync breakdown and a correctness gate.
